task_reconstruction.official_task: 2023 MCM Problem C, as restated on physical page 5.

whether word attributes affect Hard Mode percentage

contributions.summary: Abstract uses borrowed-domain analogy framing: epidemiology for game spread, KNN for distribution prediction.
Novel character-level features (regularity via Markov chain, purity via negentropy) grounded in information theory.
PCQL model extends SIR by splitting Recovered into Quitted and Loyal, capturing habitual player persistence.
Clean null result on Hard Mode: R²=0.022 plus temporal confound argument.
KNN regression exploits sum-preservation property for distributional prediction; K=15 by 10-fold CV.
KNN classifier (K=8) achieves 75.28% accuracy for 3-class difficulty classification.
Cross-model validation: Hard Mode proportion trend matches PCQL loyal-player proportion.

dependency_graph.label: PCQL loyal-player trend motivates confounding argument in regression null result.
KNN regression distributional output informs difficulty median computation which feeds classifier.

assumptions.summary: Words in the given data are English words sharing common probabilistic identities with dictionary words.
Players prefer generality: familiar-looking words are recalled first.
Consistency of Behavior: TPers do TP everyday, non-TPers never do.
Viral Marketing: conversion probability proportional to contact with active TPers.
Potential Customers: only a subset of population can become TPers.
No Return: ex-TPers never return to TP.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Two types of outliers removed: non-5-letter words and unusually low report counts.
Normalization to mean 0, variance 1 for KNN distance computation.
Regularity feature: geometric mean of bigram transition probabilities with BOW/EOW.
Purity feature: negentropy of successor character distribution.
Repetition features: count of repeated letters and maximum repetition count.
Word frequency from movie subtitle corpus (Hermit Dave).

models.summary: PCQL compartmental ODE extending SIR: 4 variables (Potential/Crowd/Quitted/Loyal), 4 parameters. Fitted via GA + Nelder-Mead, Bootstrap 95% CI [11173, 17069] for March 1 2023.
Linear regression of Hard Mode percentage on regularity. R²=0.022 (weighted), 0.013 (unweighted). Conclusion: word attributes do not meaningfully affect Hard Mode ratio.
KNN regression (K=15) using 5 word features to predict 7-bin try distribution. Cross-validated MSE=12.35. EERIE: (0.20, 4.87, 23.55, 35.36, 23.75, 9.94, 2.33). Bootstrap 95% CI.
KNN classifier (K=8) using repeated letters, weighted purity, weighted regularity. 3 difficulty levels. Accuracy 75.28%, CI [63.16%, 82.76%]. EERIE: normal.

verification.summary: GA + Nelder-Mead optimization with MSE loss. Bootstrap 1000 samples for prediction intervals.
R² and adjusted R² reported for both weighted and unweighted regularity regressions.
10-fold cross-validation for KNN regression feature and K selection. MSE=12.35.
Cross-validation for KNN classifier K selection. Accuracy 75.28% with CI [63.16%, 82.76%].
Cross-model consistency: PCQL loyal-player proportion matches Hard Mode proportion trend.

results_trace.summary: PCQL model fitted parameters: alpha=0.177, beta=0.0177, gamma=0.00104, delta=0.00114. Prediction: March 1 2023 in [11173, 17069].
R²=0.022 for weighted regularity regression: word attributes do not explain Hard Mode variation.
EERIE try distribution: (0.20, 4.87, 23.55, 35.36, 23.75, 9.94, 2.33) with ~5% prediction interval.
EERIE classified as ordinary (normal) difficulty by KNN classifier (K=8, 75.28% accuracy).
Hard Mode proportion increases over time, matching PCQL loyal-player proportion trend.

writing_logic.summary: Abstract opens with virality context-setting, then method summaries per model, closes with cross-model corroboration finding.
Memo to NYT editor: gratitude opening, lifecycle diagnosis, actionable recommendations, null-result framing, bonus insights.
Model section opens with manual EDA (shape + mechanism), reviews SIR baseline, identifies gap, extends to PCQL.
Hard Mode analysis uses dramatic section titles (It Seems True / Very Likely Not True) as narrative reversal.
KNN regression justified by sum-preservation property; two-stage feature selection (covariance then CV).
Insights section connects back to PCQL model, using temporal parallel as cross-model validation.

language_observations.summary: Abstract uses phenomenon-virality context-setting with platform exemplification: 'has been spreading widely around the world and has a high level of buzz on social media such as Twitter.'
Significance claim links domain study to broader value: 'may shed some light on important issues such as...'
Method constraint as selection criterion: 'KNN regression has the excellent property of ensuring that the predicted distribution still sums to zero.'
Memo opens with gratitude + dual-scope significance: 'important not only for your company, but also for...'
Lifecycle diagnosis from proxy: 'our epidemiology-like model tells us that Wordle has entered the tail end, or plateau, of its life cycle.'
Confound warning: 'statistical tools such as regression may misidentify this trend over time as a direct relationship.'
Double justification for model choice: shape similarity ('typical sequence') AND mechanism ('can be very viral').
Variable reinterpretation: 'we can deem S as target customers, I as score sharers, and R as those who tried and had been tired.'
Model extension motivation: 'not all the score sharers would be cured quickly; some people would pick up the habit.'
Two-stage optimization rationale: 'the formal solution is difficult to compute' + 'the time cost is high, so we choose Nelder-Mead.'
R-squared dismissal: 'only 0.022 and 0.019, which represents that the weighted regularity explains only about 2%.'
Cross-model consonance: 'this phenomenon is consistent with our PCQL Model, in which we assume that there are loyal TPers.'

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Abstract covers all four questions systematically with method + finding per paragraph.
PCQL model is creative epidemiological analogy; judges value novel cross-domain modeling.
Honest null result on Hard Mode with confound analysis shows intellectual rigor.
Cross-model validation (Hard Mode vs PCQL loyal) is a sophisticated consistency check.

weaknesses.summary: Abstract uses 'buzz' colloquially; academic papers typically avoid informal register in the summary sheet.
Section 5 title 'Is Word Itself affect Hard Mode Ratio' contains grammatical error (missing auxiliary 'Does').
Outlier data table shows 'rprobe' and 'clen' and 'tash' removed without explaining how correct words were identified.
Normalization formula uses x_ij* notation but the denominator shows sigma(x_j) without specifying whether it is standard deviation or variance.
Claim 'no periodicity under weekly frequency' cites F-test but provides no test statistic, p-value, or degrees of freedom.
'TP' and 'TPer' terminology is idiosyncratic; would benefit from clearer connection to standard epidemiology terms.
SIR review shows 3 equations but labels it 'a system of four differential equations' — the R equation is present but S+I+R=N is the implicit fourth constraint, not an equation.
PCQL model page shows transition diagram but the symbolic labels in the diagram are partially illegible in the PDF rendering.
Fitted parameters alpha=0.177, beta=0.0177, gamma=0.00104, delta=0.00114 are presented without confidence intervals or sensitivity analysis.
Bootstrap interval [11173, 17069] is wide (53% range relative to midpoint); practical prediction utility is limited.
Regression slope -0.022 is statistically significant (p=0.005) but practically negligible (R²=0.022); paper correctly identifies this but the dual-significance messaging could confuse readers.
KNN regression MSE of 12.35 is reported without units or baseline comparison.
Feature selection abbreviation key uses '&' and '!' which may not be standard notation.
EERIE predicted distribution (0.20, 4.87, 23.55, 35.36, 23.75, 9.94, 2.33) sums to 100.0 — verified internally consistent.
Only 3 words have median=6; merging with median=5 is pragmatic but the 'hard' category mixes genuinely different difficulty levels.
Cross-model validation (PCQL loyal proportion vs Hard Mode ratio) is qualitative visual similarity, not a formal statistical test.
Only 6 references for a 24-page paper is sparse; feature engineering claims lack citation support.
